text.title: Audience Segmentation Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a queryable record store with current behavioural fields exists, what the proposed dimensions are made of, and how the attractiveness inputs can be sourced — to a full segmentation, a basis or definition fix, a scoring constraint, or a skip to persona work.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there a record store — CRM, product analytics, onboarding data — whose per-user fields you could write a query against today?

branch.when: pre-launch: no customers and no interview corpus

conclusion.verdict: skip: every attractiveness cell would be unsourced — run JTBD interviews or persona-building first and return when there are records to assign

branch.when: records exist only for retained customers, or the behavioural fields are older than roughly 18 months

conclusion.verdict: skip or re-instrument first: churned and never-converted records are the segments you most need to see, and segmenting survivors returns the customers you already have, dressed as a recommendation

branch.when: a queryable record store with current per-user behavioural fields exists and no segments have been defined yet
branch.question: What do the proposed two or three dimensions consist of?

branch.when: all firmographic or demographic — company size, industry, geography, age, seniority

conclusion.verdict: revise the basis before splitting: at least one dimension must be observed behaviour (usage, purchase trigger, frequency, channel) or the job being hired for, or within-segment variance stays equal to the population's

branch.when: at least one behavioural dimension, but the segments are prose descriptions — power users, busy founders — that no query could execute

conclusion.verdict: write each segment as a runnable predicate over real fields, run it against the full table, and report the unassignable residue; keep it at or under 5% or the definitions are personas

branch.when: at least one behavioural dimension and every segment carries an executable assignment rule over fields that exist in the store

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology: MECE executable segments, six-criterion scoring with per-cell sources, bottom-up sizing, a named channel with unit cost, one primary target

branch.when: segments are already defined and the open question is which one to target
branch.question: What can actually be sourced for the six attractiveness criteria?

branch.when: sizing is available only as a percentage of a published TAM figure

conclusion.verdict: rebuild size as denominator x qualification rate x reachable share with a source per factor; a top-down percentage has no falsifiable input and survives every review unchanged

branch.when: several of the six criteria could only be filled by estimate for some segments

conclusion.verdict: score anyway, but emit unsourced cells as null and exclude them from the composite; report coverage so the reader sees which single number is worth going out to measure

branch.when: sizes decompose bottom-up, but no segment names a channel with a targeting spec and a cost per qualified contact

conclusion.verdict: name a concrete addressable channel per segment with an observed or benchmark unit cost; a definable but unaddressable segment produces zero pipeline at any budget and fails months later as campaign underperformance

branch.when: cells are sourced and the choice comes down to two close segments

conclusion.verdict: select exactly one and record the runner-up, the criterion it lost on, and both scores, so a later re-measurement flips the choice mechanically instead of reopening the debate
